record.paper_title: Open Problems in K-Stability of Fano Varieties
record.original_question: Let X be a Fano variety. The class c_1(X) determines a canonical extension 0 -> Omega_X^{[1]} -> E -> O_X -> 0. Give a purely algebraic proof that if X is K-semistable then this extension E is semistable with respect to the polarization -K_X, and that if X is K-polystable then E is polystable with respect to -K_X.

evidence.quote:
Problem 13. Let X be a Fano variety. If X is K-semistable (resp. K-polystable), give an
algebraic proof of the following: the canonical extension E is semistable (resp. polystable) with
respect to the polarization −KX.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a Fano variety (a normal projective variety over the complex numbers with -K_X an ample Q-Cartier divisor, having at worst klt singularities). Let Ω_X^{[1]} denote the sheaf of reflexive Kähler differentials on X. The first Chern class c_1(X) ∈ H^1(X, Ω_X^{[1]}) determines (via the Atiyah-style construction) a canonical extension of coherent sheaves

  0 → Ω_X^{[1]} → E → O_X → 0.

For a torsion-free coherent sheaf F on X, define its slope with respect to the polarization -K_X by μ_{-K_X}(F) = (c_1(F) · (-K_X)^{n-1}) / rk(F), where n = dim X. The sheaf F is called slope semistable (resp. polystable) with respect to -K_X if for every coherent subsheaf F' ⊂ F with 0 < rk(F') < rk(F) one has μ_{-K_X}(F') ≤ μ_{-K_X}(F) (resp. F is a direct sum of slope-stable sheaves of the same slope).

Prove, by purely algebraic methods (i.e., without invoking the existence of a Kähler-Einstein metric or other transcendental/analytic input), the following two statements:

(a) If X is K-semistable, then E is slope semistable with respect to -K_X.

(b) If X is K-polystable, then E is slope polystable with respect to -K_X.
artifact.status_search_result: The result is known via differential-geometric methods (using Kähler-Einstein metrics and Hermitian-Einstein structures on the canonical extension, following work of Tian and subsequent extensions). A purely algebraic proof, in the generality of K-(semi/poly)stable Q-Fano varieties not assumed to admit a Kähler-Einstein metric, is listed as an open problem in current surveys on K-stability and does not appear to have been resolved.

status_evidence.title: K-stability of Fano varieties: an algebro-geometric approach (Xu)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys algebraic approaches to K-stability; the algebraic (semi)stability of the canonical extension is discussed as a problem with known transcendental but not algebraic proof in full generality.
status_evidence.claim: The algebraic proof of (semi/poly)stability of the canonical extension under K-(semi/poly)stability is highlighted as an outstanding problem.

status_evidence.title: On the stability of extensions of tangent sheaves on Kähler-Einstein Fano/Calabi-Yau pairs
status_evidence.snippet: If a Fano manifold admits a Kähler-Einstein metric, then there is a natural Hermitian-Einstein metric on the extension bundle E, and E is slope polystable.
status_evidence.claim: The polystability of the canonical extension is established via Kähler-Einstein/Hermitian-Einstein analytic input, not by purely algebraic means.
